A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConCon research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additional experiments in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original ConCon experiments with neural and neuro-symbolic models, including benchmark accuracies, repeated-run statistics, learning curves, and error analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds PNN, shuffled-training, generative-replay, and ImageNet results.

M1.justification: The proposed ConCon construction, ground-truth rule, confounders, and disjoint/strict generation procedures remain unchanged. PNNs and generative replay are additional evaluated approaches, not revisions to the proposed framework.

E1.justification: V3 extends evaluation beyond synthetic ConCon to natural ImageNet images. The introduction evaluates six ImageNet classes; Appendix E adds 24 source classes grouped into six labels across three tasks. This substantially broadens the represented data and classification tasks.

E2.justification: V3 retains all nine original comparison setups, adds PNNs and shuffled training for both model families on both ConCon variants, and evaluates generative replay in Appendix D. These additions broaden comparison to growing architectures, generative replay, and a dedicated control.

E3.justification: V3 introduces shuffled cumulative training that breaks confounder-to-task alignment, task-aware PNN evaluation, and new ImageNet protocols with three sequential pairs of labels. The existing ConCon splits, accuracy metrics, memory-buffer size, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new shuffled control tests the contribution of temporal confounder alignment while retaining cumulative training. Appendix C also extends positive/negative error analyses to shuffled training and PNNs. The original convergence and error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions document five random seeds and report standard deviations in Appendix C. V3 extends the existing reporting convention to additional results without introducing a new statistical procedure or reporting an increase in repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Retained ConCon table values, including standard deviations, are unchanged. New strict-NN results include 89.5% unconfounded accuracy for shuffled training and 49.2% for PNNs, alongside retained cumulative/joint values of 72.6%/95.7%. Generative replay adds 47.73%/49.26% unconfounded accuracy on disjoint/strict. New ImageNet comparisons report 91.7% joint versus 89.3% cumulative accuracy and a 5.58-point average gap in the expanded experiment.

T1.justification: The predicate definitions, constraints, derivations, and conditions making the ground-truth rule the unique joint solution are retained. V2 Equation 4 is split into v3 Equations 4 and 5; this changes presentation, not mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the central contributions remain the logical framework, ConCon dataset, and demonstration that preventing forgetting or accumulating data can fail to prevent confounding. The additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 now acknowledges that the continual setup itself may explain part of the performance gap and explicitly notes similar joint/cumulative performance for NeSy. V3 adds interpretations of shuffled training and PNN task heads. Existing overfitting explanations and principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds brief PNN architecture information, a training-time exception for PNNs, the ResNet-18-based VAE description, and ImageNet class mappings and hyperparameter cross-references. Existing ConCon implementation details, code/data access, licenses, and datasheet information are largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 expands introductory context with shortcut-learning and confounding literature, including Geirhos, Steinmann, and Ye, and cites the added PNN and generative-replay comparators. Ribeiro's explanation paper is removed with the husky example. The central positioning of ConCon remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, replacing award-reporting and husky anecdotes with literature-based motivation and an ImageNet example. Related-work and results narratives are reworked, the impact statement moves into the main text, and the appendix organization is revised.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main layout, replaces Figure 1, and rearranges Figure 2 vertically. V2 Table 1 becomes two expanded tables; its error-analysis Figures 6–7 become Figures 6–9 with added rows. New generative-replay and ImageNet tables further change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The shuffled control addresses an important weakness in v2's central attribution: comparing 89.5% shuffled, 72.6% cumulative, and 95.7% joint strict-NN accuracy better separates temporal confounding from general cumulative-training effects. PNNs and generative replay broaden the empirical challenge, and the NeSy qualification improves interpretive accuracy. ImageNet mechanisms remain less directly established, and Table 2's blanket statement about old-task failure conflicts with its PNN rows, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial strengthening of the central evidence.
